units.translation: in some copies παρόν [being present] was introduced for the corrupt πλέον [more], to which I preferred πάλιν [again].
where ἣν παρών [being present] is said for παρῆν [was present].
about which passage it has been said under the word μόλις [scarcely].
where Schuetz rightly [reads] εἴπερ ἔσται γε [if indeed it will be].
where I restored ἔκδημός περ ὤν [being away from home], about which I spoke in the Preface to the fifth Leipzig edition p. XCVII.

where παροῦσαν ἐγγράφει [he writes her as present] is suspect. The scholiast [says] τάξον αὐτὴν ἀφανισθεῖσαν, ὡς πρὸς τὸ ἐλπίς δ᾽ ἀπέδωκεν [rank her as having vanished, as he rendered it in reference to hope], whence Canterus [conjectured] ἀποῦσαν ἐγγράφου [write her as absent], others have conjectured other things.
old Attic form of the imperfect
where Herwerden in Studia critica p. 4 conjectured that πάρεστι [is present] was introduced by a scribe's error from verse 961 in place of δόξαντα [having seemed].

as ἔνι ἔπι μέτα [in, on, with] for ἔνεστι ἔπεστι μέτεστι [is in, is on, has a share], which are accustomed to be placed in verses so that there is no need of elision: which Abresch had not noticed, when in Eum. 31 he wrote κεἰ παρ᾿ Ἑλλήνων τινὲς, ἴτων πάλῳ λαχόντες, πάρ᾽ [and if some of the Greeks, let them go having obtained by lot, are present], said for πάρεισι [they are present], which itself must be supplied in thought. Nor had the scholiast of Homer Il. 1, 174 noticed, when he approved πάρ᾽ ἔμοιγε καὶ ἄλλοι [beside me there are others too], where others rightly [read] παρ᾽ [beside].
τῇδ᾽ [here] Musgrave
where I wrote στένειν πάρα [it is possible to lament], as it is read in Euripides Alc. 342.
αὐτὸς αὐτὸν Μ [himself himself M]. Thus Hermann for πέρι [concerning].
where M in the first place [has] πάρα (παρά corr.) τε φῶς [and light is present (beside corrected)], in the second παρὰ τό [beside the].
